title: Construction of the local-annihilation subsheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $F$ any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exist a sheaf $G$ and a monomorphism $\iota:G\to F$ such that, for every open $U$ and section $s\in F(U)$, $s$ belongs to the image of $\iota(U)$ if and only if $a(s|_V)=0$ for every subopen $V\subseteq U$ and every $a\in J(V)$. No finite-type or quasi-coherence hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: For each open U, take the submodule of sections s satisfying local annihilation. Additivity, semilinearity of restrictions, and commutativity of scalars show that these submodules form a submodule presheaf. Its restrictions are the restricted maps of F.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Glue a compatible family in F. For V contained in the union and a in J(V), restrict the product a s to V intersected with each cover member. Naturality of the ideal inclusion shows that restriction of a remains an ideal section. Every such restricted product is zero. Separatedness of F gives a s = 0. Uniqueness is inherited from F. Package the resulting module presheaf and sheaf proof as G. The inclusion is sectionwise the subtype inclusion and hence mono; its image is the defining submodule.

theorem exists_annihilator_subsheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (ι : G ⟶ F), Mono ι ∧
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U)),
        s ∈ Set.range (ι.app U) ↔
          ∀ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U), ∀ a ∈ J.idealOfOpens V,
            a • F.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s = 0
